title: Best High Chairs UK
short: High chairs compared for ease of cleaning, adjustability and longevity, from budget staples to transitional chairs designed to last from birth to adulthood.
intro: A high chair's real test is how it copes after months of daily messy weaning, not how it looks in the showroom. This guide compares chairs tested by Mumsnet's parent testers over weeks and months of real family use, consulting child nutrition consultant Charlotte Stirling-Reed on safety and features.

products.name: Tripp Trapp Highchair
products.best_for: Buyers who want one chair to last from birth into adulthood
products.key_spec: Suitable from birth (with accessories) to adulthood, five-point harness, dishwasher-safe tray
products.summary: An almost 50-year-old classic that Mumsnet found continues to perform well for kids of any age, solidly built from high-quality wood. It's usable from birth with the newborn set, from six months with the baby set, and from age three into adulthood, though it doesn't recline or fold and almost every feature beyond the frame is sold separately.

specs.Materials: Beech, oak or ash wood; BPA-free plastics

pros: Exceptionally high build quality designed for longevity
Available in multiple wood types and 14 colourways
cons: Doesn't recline or fold away
Most features sold separately at extra cost
Wood cleans less easily than plastic or metal

products.name: Antilop
products.best_for: Buyers who want a reliable, no-frills chair at the lowest price
products.key_spec: Moulded plastic seat, steel click-in legs, three-point harness, assembles in under two minutes
products.summary: Mumsnet's testing found this lives up to its reputation as the king of budget highchairs, with a smooth plastic seat and steel legs that assemble in minutes and are dishwasher-safe. It's lightweight, stable and easy to take apart for storage, though there's no adjustability in height, tray distance or seat angle.

specs.Suitable from: Able to sit unaided to 3 years

pros: Easy to wipe clean and dishwasher-safe
cons: No adjustability in height, tray or seat angle
No colour options beyond the standard design
Limited lifespan (not intended beyond 15kg)

products.name: Flip Magic Fold Highchair
products.best_for: Buyers with limited kitchen space who need a chair that folds away small
products.key_spec: Folds to 7cm with one hand, 4.3kg, removable tray and wipe-clean cover
products.summary: Mumsnet's parent tester Izzy found this space-saving chair lightweight, easy to manoeuvre and foldable with a single button, praising it as offering great value for money. It's stylish and budget-friendly, though the tray isn't adjustable so smaller babies may struggle to reach it, and the harness strap can be fiddly.
pros: Folds to just 7cm with one hand
cons: Tray isn't adjustable
Harness can be fiddly to adjust
Unpadded seat
products.search: Ickle Bubba Flip Magic Fold Highchair

products.name: Minla Plus Evolutionary Highchair
products.best_for: Buyers who want to easily move the chair around the kitchen
products.key_spec: Birth to 14 years, wheels, pivoting tray, water-repellent EcoCare fabric
products.summary: Tested for just over six months by Mumsnet parent-tester Ally with her baby from six months to a year old, who particularly liked how easy it was to move around the kitchen on its wheels. The pivoting tray swings out to one side for getting baby in and out, and it converts from reclinable infant seat to booster usable up to age 14, though it's relatively pricey.
pros: Pivoting tray simplifies getting baby in and out
Easy to move and fold for storage
cons: Relatively pricey
Some seat cover areas can't be removed for washing

products.name: Gourmet Highchair
products.best_for: Buyers who want a premium look that still performs practically
products.key_spec: Arrives fully assembled, 5-point harness, adjustable height and recline, 15kg max load
products.summary: Mumsnet's parent-tester Tamsin praised the beautiful design and practicality, finding it easy to get her seven-month-old in and out thanks to the removable tray and secure harness. Multiple height and recline settings let it grow with your child, though the detailed stitching is hard to clean and it's heavy and bulky when stored.
cons: Detailed stitching and tray parts hard to clean
Heavy and not easily portable
Bulky when stored

products.name: Steps Highchair
products.best_for: Buyers who want a supportive, adjustable seat that grows well beyond toddlerhood
products.key_spec: 6 months to 10 years, adjustable footrest and seat, tool-free adjustments, 5-point harness included
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Holly used this daily with her son from six to eight months old and found it sturdy with a generously sized tray great for exploring food. The seat and footrest adjust without tools as your child grows, and it converts into a regular chair later, though it takes up a fair amount of kitchen space.

specs.Materials: European beechwood, plastic, fabric Baby Set

pros: Grows with your child up to 85kg
Large tray for eating and messy play
cons: Takes up quite a bit of space
Fabric Baby Set isn't the quickest to clean

products.name: Lemo Highchair 4-in-1
products.best_for: Buyers who want a single chair to last from birth well into adulthood
products.key_spec: Birth to adulthood, aluminium frame, wheels on rear feet, six colourways
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Alex found this chair easily adapted to fit a newborn, a weaning-aged baby, a toddler and even an adult, calling it usable 'birth to 99 years'. It's an elegant, stylish choice that stayed easy to keep clean across different size settings, though it's pricey and heavy, taking up significant floor space.
cons: Expensive
Heavy and large, not ideal for smaller spaces

products.name: Pocket Snack Highchair
products.best_for: Buyers who need a compact chair for visiting family or eating away from home
products.key_spec: Straps to a dining chair, folds to handbag size, dishwasher-safe tray, 15kg max
products.summary: Mumsnet's top pick for travel, folding down to handbag size with a shoulder strap for easy transport, and usable from six months to about three years. It attaches securely to a dining chair with two robust straps and has a dishwasher-safe tray for quick clean-ups, though it can't be used without an adult chair and doesn't recline.
pros: Folds down to handbag size with shoulder strap
Adjustable height and tray distance as child grows
cons: Requires an adult dining chair to attach to
Seat doesn't recline
Bright plastic look won't suit every taste

guide.q: Budget, multi-functional or transitional highchair: which type do I need?
guide.a: A budget standalone chair like the IKEA Antilop here covers the essentials cheaply but lacks adjustability. A multi-functional chair like the Maxi-Cosi Minla Plus or Silver Cross Gourmet here adds features like reclining, height adjustment and folding for storage. A transitional chair like the Stokke Tripp Trapp or Cybex Lemo here is the priciest option but converts from a baby seat into a chair that lasts into adulthood.

guide.q: When can my baby start using a highchair?
guide.a: Child nutrition consultant Charlotte Stirling-Reed advises your baby needs to be sitting in an upright position and able to hold their head and neck steady before starting, which is usually from around six months. Always sit with your baby when offering food, especially finger foods, and never leave them unattended in a highchair.

guide.q: What safety features should I check for?
guide.a: Look for the EU safety directive EN 14988:2017, which sets specific standards for children's highchairs. Beyond that, Charlotte Stirling-Reed recommends checking the height of the seat back for support, whether the harness is a secure three- or five-point design, how solidly the tray attaches, and whether a footrest is included to stop your child slumping.

guide.q: Do I need a travel highchair as well as one at home?
guide.a: If you regularly visit family or friends without a highchair, or eat out often, a compact travel chair like the Chicco Pocket Snack here is genuinely useful and easy to pack. Most attach to an adult dining chair with straps, though it's worth checking compatibility with the furniture you'll actually be using it on.
